name: ID-02
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's R+13 partisan lean anchors the race firmly in Republican territory
Simpson's incumbency and roughly 10-to-1 fundraising edge over Gilbreath
Prediction markets price the Democratic chance at only about 4 percent
No public general-election polling, leaving fundamentals as the main guide
model.rationale: Simpson combines a safe R+13 seat, long incumbency, and a dominant financial position, while markets give Gilbreath only a token chance and no polling suggests a competitive race. The fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-teens, consistent with the quantitative baseline.
model.watch: Any late outside spending on Gilbreath or an unexpected development involving Simpson could tighten the race, though no such signals have appeared.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Simpson seeks another term in a heavily Republican eastern Idaho district that leans about thirteen points toward the GOP. He has raised more than $1.1 million and holds a large cash advantage over Democrat Ellie Gilbreath, who has raised roughly $107,000. Two independents and a Libertarian are also on the ballot, likely splitting minor protest votes rather than mounting serious campaigns.

No public general-election polls exist for this race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give the Democratic side only about a four percent chance of an upset. The expected outcome is a comfortable Simpson victory in the mid-teens, with modest uncertainty because polling is absent and the national political environment could shift turnout patterns at the margins.
